news.title: Opinion | A FIFA World Cup and a Village's Stolen Dream
news.lede: In the middle of the global celebration of football, when stadiums are full, screens are glowing, and millions are watching the World Cup, a small Palestinian village near Bethlehem experienced something very different.Battir lost its only football field.For most of the world, football is entertainment. In Battir, it is something else entirely—it is space, identity, and a rare place where young people can breathe beyond the pressures of daily life.The field was not a stadium. It had no grandstands, no giant screens, and no professional facilities. It was a simple community pitch.

news.title: Gianni Infantino 'certain to go' according to FIFA insiders after botched World Cup plot
news.lede: Gianni Infantino looks certain to be ousted as FIFA President after his 'shabby' attempts to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors. Infantino, 56, could have profited from the "Fifa Forward Enterprise" scheme (FFE) and is trying to stay in his post. But his support is flooding away. A source told the Sunday Times that Infantino is a 'dead duck' while opponents were reportedly lining up candidates as his successor.

news.title: FIFA scrap World Cup sell-off plan after backlash
news.lede: This content is provided by Exco Player and may use cookies or similar technologies. Please click 'Allow and Continue' below to load the content. FIFA “will not proceed” with plans to sell stakes in a company which would run the commercial and operational aspects of its competitions, a statement from president Gianni Infantino said. The plan, which would include the men’s and women’s World Cups, has been rejected by three continental confederations with UEFA insisting its nations would boycott FIFA events.

news.title: UEFA to boycott World Cup if Infantino sell-off plan goes ahead
news.lede: This content is provided by Exco Player and may use cookies or similar technologies. Please click 'Allow and Continue' below to load the content. England, its fellow UEFA nations and CONCACAF have unanimously voted to boycott the upcoming men’s and women’s World Cups if Gianni Infantino goes ahead with plans to sell off shares in the tournament to private investors. UEFA’s 55 member nations held a virtual crisis meeting on Thursday to discuss Infantino’s recently announced plans to privatise and sell shares in the World Cup.

news.title: FIFA boss Infantino’s position looks unacceptable: European Leagues head
news.lede: Who is tipped to replace Gianni Infantino after the World Cup investment plan crisis? UEFA, who were the strongest opponents of FIFA’s plan, slam the Gianni Infantino-led governing body despite standdown. Asian Football Confederation says FIFA future must be ‘shaped through proper consultation’ after World Cup plan fallout. How FIFA President Gianni Infantino was forced abandon his World Cup equity plan after seismic backlash across football.

news.title: Buffon reveals who he would have chosen as Italy head coach: ‘World Cup main goal’
news.lede: Gianluigi Buffon has spoken about the offer he received to return to the Italy national team set-up under Paolo Maldini, has explained why it is important to have a figure like Claudio Ranieri involved and has revealed who he would have chosen instead of Roberto Mancini as the next head coach. The legendary former goalkeeper and former Italy delegation chief spoke all things Nazionale in an in-depth interview with La Gazzetta dello Sport, published on Sunday. It has been a hectic few weeks for the Italy national team and its supporters. Maldini was appointed as the new technical director of the FIGC only to resign just over a fortnight later.

news.title: Football Ferns legend breaks silence on controversial call to miss 2023 Women's World Cup
news.lede: Reminder, this is a Premium article and requires a subscription to read. Former Football Ferns captain Abby Erceg, pictured during one of her last international appearances. Former Football Ferns captain Abby Erceg has no regrets over her absence from the 2023 Fifa Women’s World Cup in New Zealand and Australia, even if it was one of the toughest decisions of her career. Erceg, who will feature as a guest player for Auckland FC’s invitational team against Chelsea Women on Saturday at Eden Park, was the biggest name missing from Jitka Klimkova’s squad three years ago.

news.title: Ranking World Cup performances by Bayern Munich players
news.lede: From 1982 to 2022, every single FIFA World Cup Final featured at least one Bayern Munich player. That streak came to an end in 2026, as France lost to Spain and England lost to Argentina in the semifinals. However, that doesn’t mean that Bayern didn’t have plenty of representation in the World Cup. Today, we’re taking a look at Bayern Munich’s World Cup performances from worst to best (Nathaniel Brown and Ismael Saibari are not included as they only joined Bayern midway through the tournament).
